across: rurality (affected city vs rural counties' clinics)

ev.q: to 80.0% of owners compared with 8.3% before the outbreak
Responding rural clinics reported recommending vaccination more frequently than did clinics in the affected city

changes.why: The report sets rural-county clinics against affected-city clinics in its own words, and rurality is a listed social-position dimension, so it belongs in across; the pre/post contrast stays primary and values are only set side by side.

equity.level_reason: Clinic-reported canine vaccination results are given separately for rural-county and affected-city clinics and described (rural clinics recommend more, with higher owner compliance), but not framed as a disparity or quantified as a contrast.

level_alternative.reason: The rural vs city split is really outbreak-affected vs unaffected geography about dogs' vaccination, not a social position of people; occupation is a route of exposure, not SES.

ev.q: Six of 10 clinics in the affected city and eight clinics in rural counties responded.
approximately 50%–60% of dogs in rural clinics were reported as vaccinated both pre- and postoutbreak

equity.equity_measurement: Rurality is a clinic-level label (rural counties vs the affected city) from a small voluntary survey (6 of 10 city clinics, 8 rural clinics) reporting estimated percentages of dogs and owners.

notes: Other fields of the structural record are acceptable; data_focus 'yes' is defensible given the 13-dog case series and the pre/post clinic survey. 'Vaccine-preventable (other)' rests on canine vaccines only; no human vaccine exists.
